rubric_additions.rubric-11:
Rule: Check which setting actually wins when the Python app is started, for example --reload versus FLASK_RUN_RELOAD.
Example: make dev supplies --reload, so FLASK_RUN_RELOAD=false alone does not establish a single-process run.
Evidence: Scope and required checks: Check the Python runner's effective precedence. FLASK_RUN_RELOAD=false does not override an explicit --reload in make dev. To claim no reload, use a supported flag or configuration that actually wins. Otherwise limit the evidence to the real reload worker and process-group cleanup. Preserve existing reload policy unless a change was selected. An environment assignment alone does not prove single-process startup.
Insufficient evidence: An environment assignment that loses to the actual runner flag.
rubric_additions.rubric-12:
Rule: For selected Python metric-reader settings, preserve supported fractional values and the SDK's handling of invalid or empty input.
Example: A supported fractional metric interval must not be rejected by a new integer-only wrapper.
Evidence: Short-run timing defaults belong to the selected launch policy, not the SDK's defaults.
Insufficient evidence: A custom parsing rule or short-run launch value presented as the SDK default.
rubric_additions.rubric-13:
Rule: For a selected Python zero-code CLI, inspect the installed exporter-list reader and the transport chosen by each alias.
Example: An explicit OTLP alias can choose a transport even when the generic protocol variable names another transport. Inspect the installed alias owner.
Evidence: An explicit OTLP alias may choose its transport independently of protocol environment settings. Valid mixed lists containing supported OTLP members must receive approval and header checks. Plan or run the selected conflict and approved signal-specific endpoint A with unused generic endpoint B through the normal command. Remove only added OTLP members when isolating a conflict, preserving other exporters and their bridge. Preserve the installed SDK's treatment of whole-value none, letter case, empty members and duplicates. Keep source-proven unsupported combinations explicit; do not substitute another language's normalization or a new parser.
Insufficient evidence: Another language's list normalization, or a mixed-list conflict path that discards unrelated exporters.
rubric_additions.rubric-22:
Rule: If a selected Python log output is created lazily, it is fine to set it up with the standard logging library's public configuration, as long as each producer's real route exists before the root bridge is installed.
Example: A framework native handler may be created lazily; public logger/handler setup must establish that route before the root bridge changes it.
Evidence: Scope and required checks: For selected Python native sinks initialized lazily, public standard-library logger/handler configuration is valid when it establishes each producer's actual route before installing a root bridge. Private initialization code can explain the lazy behavior. Calling a private underscored initializer solely to trigger setup or emit a diagnostic does not prove a supported bootstrap or preservation of the native sink.
Insufficient evidence: Calling a private initializer just to create the observed sink or diagnostic.
rubric_additions.rubric-25:
Rule: The untouched Python fixture hands app.logger.warning to an executor without copying the request context. Plan, repair or check that handoff, according to your role.
Example: The fixture submits app.logger.warning to an executor without copying the caller context. A selected fix must exercise that real handoff.
Evidence: Audit must plan acceptance checks for that missing handoff. Instrumentation repairs it if it is still missing. Verification checks the current real request-to-async SDK-context join without editing code. An already repaired path is not a remaining missing-transfer defect.
Insufficient evidence: A standalone context-copy test without the real request-to-executor log join.
rubric_additions.rubric-27:
Rule: The Python fixture's operator privacy policy covers existing exported HTTP SERVER spans as well as selected logs.
Example: Sanitizing log records does not remove a sensitive path still present in an exported HTTP SERVER span.
Evidence: A logs-only sanitizer cannot prove span privacy. Match sensitive path/query and escaping-error cases to their actual producers and supported sanitization points. Audit retains source-supported repairs and future checks. Instrumentation and verification retain current normal-launch received server-span assertions and selected log evidence. Do not add payload/header capture, extra exception telemetry or blanket suppression. This fixture policy is not a universal OpenTelemetry ban on exception messages or stacks.
Insufficient evidence: Log-only redaction used to claim privacy for selected server spans.
rubric_additions.rubric-28:
Rule: For the Python fixture's selected HTTP privacy path, preserve the required bounded error category, method/route/status, trace context and Resource identity.
Example: An error response may be private yet lose its bounded category or typed status when the message is replaced wholesale.
Evidence: Use actual structured producer fields or message-template arguments with their original types. Normalize decorations only when their source is verified. For every selected non-success, access or error operation, assert both its native and exported category and the required typed fields.
Insufficient evidence: A safe substring without the selected operation's native/exported category and required typed fields.
rubric_additions.rubric-30:
Rule: For a selected Python attribute sanitizer, inspect a downstream record after the actual callback.
Example: Replacing an SDK attribute container with a plain dictionary can erase a dropped-attribute count already accumulated by that record.
Evidence: Replacing an SDK attribute container with a plain mapping can erase existing dropped-attribute counts; that is not unchanged default behavior. Use the owner's supported mutation or snapshot mechanism without inventing counters. Rebuilding a parent span does not preserve each event's own attribute limits or accumulated dropped-attribute count.
Insufficient evidence: A parent-span rebuild or visible-value check used to claim each event's limit/drop-state preservation.
rubric_additions.rubric-36:
Rule: A selected Python metric reader's collection timeout does not automatically set its transport timeout or the application's stop budget.
Example: A metric reader's collection deadline may differ from the exporter request deadline and the application stop budget.
Evidence: Assess each claimed budget at its actual owner.
Insufficient evidence: One timeout value used to claim all three independently owned budgets.
rubric_additions.rubric-43:
Rule: In Python standard logging, a handler can prevent lastResort fallback even when that handler rejects the record.
Example: A rejecting handler can still prevent Python lastResort fallback, even when the bridge excludes that SDK logger namespace.
Evidence: Excluding SDK namespaces from the bridge therefore does not prove native diagnostics still work. Inspect an eligible handler or supported suppression on the actual SDK logger namespace. A sibling application/framework handler or another internal recursion logger cannot prove that route. If an adequate route or source-supported suppression already exists, do not require a new handler or a newly emitted diagnostic.
Insufficient evidence: An excluded namespace or unrelated sibling handler used as proof of the actual SDK diagnostic route.
rubric_additions.rubric-51:
Rule: For a selected manually constructed Python metric reader, omitted timing keyword arguments are not missing configuration wiring when the installed constructor itself reads the supported environment settings.
Example: Omitting a timing keyword is valid when the installed metric-reader constructor consumes the supported environment value itself.
Evidence: Inspect the selected installed constructor and its supported environment reader before treating an omitted timing argument as missing wiring.
Insufficient evidence: Treating an omitted keyword as missing wiring without inspecting the actual constructor.
rubric_additions.rubric-58:
Rule: If a selected Python repair adds a local-development launch profile, match its logs host, port and path to an independently approved destination.
Example: A local profile may use a loopback alias only when preflight independently approved that alias, port and path.
Evidence: Plan or prove that the profile's defaults activate the selected logging pipeline through that same launcher; choosing an OTLP exporter alone does not prove activation. Keep an unapproved host spelling as a negative test: loopback aliases are not automatically interchangeable approvals. An alias is valid when preflight independently approves it. Judge profile/approval agreement here without repeating credential or Resource identity checks.
Insufficient evidence: Choosing an OTLP exporter or any loopback host without proving the selected profile's approval and activation agreement.
rubric_additions.rubric-61:
Rule: If the selected Python CLI launcher uses a Python helper, plan or test its absence and failure without stopping the application.
Example: A host with python3 but no python alias can use the normal approved route; explicit none or console still starts when neither helper name is available.
Evidence: Audit plans these controls; instrumentation and verification execute them only when this launcher is selected and within role permissions. Bind helper availability and exit status to the actual command. Failed helper output must not authorize unchecked OTLP. Preserve original application arguments, exit result, native sinks and trace/metric settings. If a mixed OTLP list cannot be safely filtered without a working helper, keep its invocation-only log-export limitation explicit rather than claiming all operator exporters remain active. Do not persist a normal opt-out or invent an installed-SDK or telemetry result from a fake command interface.
Insufficient evidence: A successful helper-only probe, a bare-python assumption, unchecked OTLP after helper failure, or an application that never started.
